name: Prince Buster
hook: A Kingston sound-system man and ska producer whose songs gave Madness its name and the Specials their first single.

blurb.age13: Prince Buster was born Cecil Campbell in Kingston in 1938. He worked for Coxsone Dodd's sound system, then started his own, Voice of the People, and made ska records in the early 1960s. His song 'Al Capone' was a hit in Britain in 1967. Twelve years later a London band named themselves Madness after one of his songs, and a Coventry band, the Specials, built their first single on 'Al Capone'.
blurb.adult: Born Cecil Bustamente Campbell in Kingston in 1938, named for the labour leader Alexander Bustamante. After working for Coxsone Dodd's sound system he set up his own, Voice of the People, which became a rival to Dodd's and Duke Reid's, and he recorded and produced ska from the early 1960s. 'Madness' (1963) and 'Al Capone' (1964, UK number 18 in February 1967) were both carried to Britain by Jamaican migration and the mod and skinhead audiences of the 1960s, which is how they reached the 2 Tone generation. He died in 2016.
